implemented: Home: 'Approvals and alerts' (Requests unavailable) and 'Agent controls' (Status unavailable) rows under Agent tasks

Approvals: 'Approval requests unavailable', stated as not an empty list; when a payment waits (above the review threshold, held up to 15 minutes, nothing paid without approval on the protected screen); reject or expiry makes no signature and releases the reservation; guide for Pending, Approved, Rejected and Expired; link to Alerts; __DEV__-only samples, pending and expired only (no approved sample)

Approval detail (development samples only): amount in display and base units, time left, from (Agent wallet), network and chain, action, provider, full recipient address (words), asset, task, review threshold; agent's reason tagged 'Untrusted model text'; 'Payment check on this phone: Not built'; Approve and Reject disabled; reject sends no signature; an expired request shows it can no longer be decided

Alerts: 'Alerts unavailable'; the service hold is off chain and is not a freeze; only the owner clears it after signing in again; __DEV__-only sample alert with wallet, network, rule, detection, service hold and 'Frozen on chain: Unavailable'; Freeze and Clear hold disabled

Agent controls: agent wallet state (account, network, frozen, paused, service hold) all unavailable, never shown as stopped; a stop counts once confirmed and earlier payments may settle; separate cards for Freeze and Unfreeze (permissions kept), Pause and Revoke (authority ends; unpause does not restore), and Log out (service session only, agents keep working); each card states its scope (on chain or service session) and its effect on existing permissions; every action disabled
config/approvals.ts labels every shared ApprovalRequest state and Operation; canDecide and expiryLabel; config/agentControls.ts ties each on-chain control to Person1's AdminCommand number
fixtures: config/approvalSamples.ts: one pending and one expired sample request and one sample alert, shown only in __DEV__ builds and always labelled. Expiry times are relative to app load so the countdown reads sensibly. Addresses are words, never hex. There is deliberately no approved sample.
